characterList.description: A round, yellow bacterium with a bumpy surface, depicted with a face showing angry eyes and red lips in some scenes.
characterList.name: Staphylococcus aureus

content_metadata.description: The video explains how the second messenger c-di-AMP inhibits the osmolyte uptake system OpuC in Staphylococcus aureus, focusing on its role in regulating osmotic protection.

qAndA.question: What are the four proteins involved in early salt tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus?
Which molecule specifically binds to the CBS domain of the OpuCA protein?

qAndA.answer: It shows more carnitine molecules being transported into the wild-type cell with normal c-di-AMP levels, while fewer carnitine molecules enter the mutant cell with increased c-di-AMP.
qAndA.question: How does the visualization demonstrate the difference in carnitine uptake between wild-type and mutant cells?

qAndA.answer: X-ray crystallography, visualized by the appearance of a crystal and the protein structure.
qAndA.question: What method was used to elucidate the structure of the OpuCA protein?

qAndA.answer: The second messenger c-di-AMP plays a crucial role in regulating osmotic protection in Staphylococcus aureus by inhibiting the activity of the OpuC transporter responsible for taking up osmolytes like carnitine. This knowledge could be applied in future strategies to prevent foodborne Staphylococcus aureus infections.

text_to_speech: Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive bacterium that is about two micrometers in size and can be found on the skin of about thirty percent of the population. Although often benign it can cause endocarditis, toxic shock syndrome, skin infections, sepsis, and other illnesses. Staphylococcus aureus is also common foodborne pathogen found it meat and meat products. Widespread methods to preserve foods are the use of excess amounts of sugar or salt to dehydrate the products. This can prevent bacterial growth and hence the transmission of foods spoilage organisms. Staphylococcus aureus however is exceptionally resistant to high salt concentrations and therefore can survive these processes better than many other organisms. Recent work in Staphylococcus aureus has revealed a second messenger called cyclic-di-AMP, that interacts with several proteins that target early salt tolerance genes. These are KtrA, a potassium transporter KdpD, a sensor histidine kinase potentially involved in potassium uptake CpaA, another protein supposedly involved in cation transport but also PstA, a protein of unknown function. In our recent study, we were able to identify an additional target of cyclic di-AMP in Staphylococcus aureus, the ABC transporter component OpuCA. The OpuC ABC transporter consists of OpuCA, the ATPase component that provides energy for the transport. OpuCB and OpuCD, the main transporter components involved in translocation of the substrates and OpuCC, the substrate binding protein responsible for the specificity This transporter is supposedly involved in the uptake of osmolytes and this can help Staphylococcus aureus to cope with osmotic stresses. Binding of cyclic d-AMP occurs via the CBS domain of OpuCA and this binding is specific for the nucleotide cyclic-di-AMP. Other nucleotides such as ATP, AMP or cyclic-AMP are unable to out-compete binding of cyclic-di-AMP. With the help of X-ray crystallography, we were able to eludicate the structure of OpuCA as depicted here. By comparison to MJ01000, a structurally related protein colored in blue, we can make educated guesses were c-di-AMP could be binding. Exchange of important amino acids and subsequent binding testing revealed that the proposed binding site is likely the functional region. Further experiments revealed that the OpuC transporter is able to transport carnitine, whereas glycine betaine and choline are not taken up in significant amounts. When cyclic-di-AMP levels were increased in the cell, the uptake of Ccarnitine was reduced compared to wild-type cells. Taken together, our research highlights the role of cyclic di AMP as a regulator of osmotic stresses. This knowledge may help in the future to prevent foodborne Staph aureus infections. More information can be found in the paper "The second messenger cycli di-AMP inhibits the osmolyte uptake system OpuC in Staphylococcus aureus", by Schuster and Bellows et al., published in Science Signaling, vol.9 issue 441 on August 16th, 2016 Thank you for watching!
